papers.title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
papers.summary: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.

papers.title: VASSO: Variance Suppression for Sharpness-Aware Minimization
papers.summary: Sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) has well-documented merits in enhancing generalization of deep neural network models. Accounting for sharpness in the loss function geometry, where neighborhoods of `flat minima' heighten generalization ability, SAM seeks `flat valleys' by minimizing the maximum loss provoked by an adversarial perturbation within the neighborhood. Although critical to account for sharpness of the loss function, in practice SAM suffers from `over-friendly adversaries,' which can curtail the outmost level of generalization. To avoid such `friendliness,' the present contribution fosters stabilization of adversaries through variance suppression (VASSO). VASSO offers a general approach to provably stabilize adversaries. In particular, when integrating VASSO with SAM, improved generalizability is numerically validated on extensive vision and language tasks. Once applied on top of a computationally efficient SAM variant, VASSO offers a desirable generalization-computation tradeoff.

papers.title: Growing a Neural Network in Breadth, Depth, and Time
papers.summary: Brains and AI systems alike must achieve their goals with limited space, time, energy, and data. Here we focus on space and time, defining differentiable costs for breadth (channels), depth (layers), and time (recurrent steps) in a recurrent convolutional network. We find that breadth, depth, and time can be traded off against each other at a given level of accuracy. papers.title: Cross-Attack Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning
papers.summary: Federated learning (FL) lets resource-constrained IoT and edge devices train a shared model without exchanging raw data, but compromised or faulty devices can poison the global model. papers.title: CoCoNet: Convex Conformal Network for Multi-Dimensional Uncertainty Regions
papers.summary: Conformal prediction (CP) provides distribution-free coverage guarantees under exchangeability, but the efficiency of its prediction regions depends critically on the choice of the conformity score. This is particularly important in multivariate regression, where dependencies across output dimensions induce complex joint uncertainty structures. This paper introduces CoCoNet (Convex Conformal Network) for learning conformity scores that induce flexible and data-adaptive prediction regions. The main mechanism is an input-dependent convex score learned end-to-end: CoCoNet trains the score on held-out data by directly minimizing the size of its sublevel sets, while enforcing convexity with respect to the residual so that every prediction region is inherently convex. CoCoNet then applies split-conformal calibration to retain finite-sample coverage guarantees. The paper presents two variants of the method: 1) CoCoNet-Spline, based on piecewise-linear scores aggregated by an $\ell_\infty$ or an $\ell_1$ norm, which induce hyper-rectangular and polytope prediction regions, respectively; and 2) CoCoNet-ICNN, based on Input Convex Neural Networks, which induces more flexible convex regions. Experiments compare CoCoNet with other CP baselines over synthetic and real-world datasets with output dimensions ranging from 2 to 16. These results demonstrate the importance of learning input-adaptive conformity scores directly from the data.

papers.title: Parasite Features: Causal Abstraction Through Spurious Pathways
papers.summary: Causal Abstraction defines a notion of \emph{equivalence} between a neural network and an algorithm, thus serving as a powerful framework for mechanistic interpretability. In this paper, however, we show the existence of a class of \emph{spurious features} which straightforwardly pass such equivalence tests. Suppose there are two directions in a model's representation space where: (i) one discriminates the input based on some feature, and (ii) the other steers the model towards a certain output. Interpretability methods based on Causal Abstraction (e.g., Distributed Alignment Search) can \emph{spuriously} simulate these directions' combined behavior by leveraging pathways passing through them, giving the impression that the model implements this feature. In such cases, we say the method discovered a \defn{parasite feature}. Experimentally, we show that Distributed Alignment Search finds parasite features using linear alignment maps in two tasks: syntactic agreement and two-digit addition. Our paper highlights an important consideration for Causal Abstraction and contributes to the ongoing debate about best practices for mechanistic interpretability.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Robust Resonance Mass Regression in Cascade Decays
papers.summary: Reconstructing the mass of a heavy resonance from its decay products with missing energy is one of the central tasks that directly determine the sensitivity in new physics searches at collider experiments. papers.title: Similarity Pairing with Energy Mover's Distance for Self-Supervised Pre-Training at the LHC
papers.summary: Many self-supervised methods for training foundation models at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) rely on data augmentations to encourage the model to embed events into a representation space invariant to certain physical or detector symmetries. A common challenge arises from the large freedom in choosing a proper set of augmentations on which downstream performance depends. The implementation of augmentations involves either modifying existing events, potentially breaking the event fidelity, or simulating more event variants, which is computationally intensive. In this work, we present a data-driven method of pairing events by their similarity via the energy mover's distance (EMD), which measures how similar two events are in terms of the work required to transform one into the other. With this approach, distinct events are sampled and matched by their similarity to serve as views for learning invariance, keeping the physics content of each event intact without handcrafted distortions. We demonstrate this augmentation-free pairing method by pre-training on QCD jets via self-distillation and show that it can yield semantic jet embeddings with downstream discrimination power comparable to or better than an augmentation-based baseline.

papers.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
papers.summary: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

papers.title: Designing Algorithmic Recommendations to Achieve Human-AI Complementarity
papers.summary: Algorithms frequently assist, rather than replace, human decision-makers. However, the design and analysis of algorithms often focus on predicting outcomes and do not explicitly model their effect on human decisions. This discrepancy between the design and role of algorithmic assistants becomes particularly concerning in light of empirical evidence that suggests that algorithmic assistants again and again fail to improve human decisions. In this article, we formalize the design of recommendation algorithms that assist human decision-makers without making restrictive ex-ante assumptions about how recommendations affect decisions. We formulate an algorithmic-design problem that leverages the potential-outcomes framework from causal inference to model the effect of recommendations on a human decision-maker's binary treatment choice. Within this model, we make a connection between algorithmic recommendations and instrumental variables. Leveraging this connection, we introduce a monotonicity assumption that leads to an intuitive classification of human responses to the algorithm. Under this assumption, we can express the human's response to algorithmic recommendations in terms of their compliance with the algorithm and the active decision they would take if the algorithm sends no recommendation. We showcase the utility of our framework using an online experiment that simulates a hiring task. We argue that our approach can make sense of the relative performance of different recommendation algorithms in the experiment and can help design solutions that realize human-AI complementarity. Finally, we leverage our approach to derive maximin-optimal recommendation algorithms that can be implemented with machine learning using limited training data.

papers.title: RNAGenScape: Property-Guided, Optimized Generation of mRNA Sequences with Manifold Langevin Dynamics
papers.summary: Generating property-optimized mRNA sequences is central to applications such as vaccine design and protein replacement therapy, but remains challenging due to limited data, complex sequence-function relationships, and the narrow space of biologically viable sequences. By performing iterative local optimization constrained to this manifold, RNAGenScape preserves favorable computational viability proxies, accesses reliable guidance, and discourages excursions into regions poorly supported by the training data. Across three real-world mRNA datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size, RNAGenScape increases median oracle-predicted property gain by up to 267% and success rate by up to 31%, while maintaining good biological viability proxy measures and achieving competitive inference efficiency compared to existing generative approaches.

papers.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
papers.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. Here we introduce Rapids, a streaming neural decoder that is both fast and accurate. papers.title: Sequential Anytime Valid Tests for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment
papers.summary: Inference-time alignment methods, such as Best-of-N (BoN), improve language model outputs by generating multiple candidates per prompt and selecting among them using a reward model. We instead seek an anytime-valid stopping rule that takes an error tolerance $α$ as input and halts only once an answer is certified to hold a majority ($θ_a > 1/2$) under the generator's distribution. We aggregate candidates by final answer with a reward-weighted self-consistency (RWSC) score and treat stopping as a sequential test over the resulting clusters. Applying Wald's sequential probability ratio test to these clusters yields SPRT-RWSC, which performs well empirically, but its guarantee fails because the leading answer shifts during sampling, and the run is continuously monitored. Our main contribution, e-RWSC, replaces Wald's test with a betting supermartingale (an e-process) for every answer the policy produces, bounding the probability of ever certifying a non-dominant answer by $α$, uniformly over time and across all answers. The RWSC scores drive the bets, so they affect only how quickly a dominant answer $a^\star$ is certified, not validity; certification takes $O(\log(1/α)/d_{\mathrm{KL}}(θ_{a^\star}\|1/2))$ samples. papers.title: The Dichotomy Between Pattern Recognition and Step-by-Step Reasoning
papers.summary: We argue that pattern recognition and step-by-step reasoning are two ends of a spectrum. A large language model (LLM) learns to reason step-by-step when data is structured such that the next token depends on a small amount of preceding context. Inference in LLMs resembles pattern recognition when the next token depends on a large amount of preceding context. If the next token depends on only the $c$ most recent tokens, reasoning traces are paths on a de Bruijn graph whose nodes are $c$-length contexts and edges are next-token transitions between contexts. The set of reasoning traces of a task forms a directed acyclic subgraph of the de Bruijn graph. An LLM that has learned all edges of this subgraph can compose them to solve longer, unseen tasks, i.e., it reasons step-by-step. We prove that the number of edges is vanishingly small compared to the number of reasoning traces. We also prove and show empirically that the number of training samples a transformer needs is a linear in the number of edges, so learning to reason step-by-step is sample efficient. We can induce de Bruijn structure in any task by maintaining a ``state'' that makes future reasoning independent of the past. The frequency of states in the reasoning trace determines $c$. We show, by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct to solve equations and answer questions about stories, that frequent states (small $c$) result in higher accuracy but greater fragility to perturbations at test time. LLMs trained with a large $c$ are only as good as models that perform pattern recognition without reasoning. A moderate density of states balances accuracy and robustness. Real-world data has de Bruijn structure: Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B retain over 75\% of their accuracy on GSM8K, MATH-500 and GPQA-Diamond when attention is restricted to a sliding window less than 15\% as long as the full reasoning trace.

papers.title: Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs with Quantum Local Differential Privacy
papers.summary: When sensitive information is encoded in data, it is important to ensure the privacy of information when attempting to learn useful information from the data. There is a natural tradeoff whereby increasing privacy requirements may decrease the utility of a learning protocol. We then study the specific application of learning the expectation of an observable with respect to an input state when only given access to privatized states. We derive a lower bound on the number of samples of privatized data required to achieve a fixed accuracy guarantee with high probability. To prove this result, we employ existing lower bounds on private quantum hypothesis testing, thus showcasing the first operational use of them. We also devise private mechanisms that achieve optimal sample complexity with respect to the privacy parameters and accuracy parameters, demonstrating that utility can be significantly improved for specific tasks in contrast to the generic setting. In addition, we show that the number of samples required to privately learn observable expectation values scales as $Θ((\varepsilon β)^{-2})$, where $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ is the privacy parameter and $β$ is the accuracy tolerance. We conclude by initiating the study of private classical shadows, which promise useful applications for private learning tasks.

papers.title: A Complete Geometric Message-Passing Architecture for Point Clouds
papers.summary: Three-dimensional point clouds are a fundamental data modality, and a large family of machine learning architectures has been developed to respect their natural symmetries to rigid motions and permutations. papers.title: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity
papers.summary: Attention heads specialize into distinct functions during training, often emerging in stages together with sharp changes in model behavior. papers.title: Learning Multinomial Logits in $O(n \log n)$ time
papers.summary: A Multinomial Logit (MNL) model is composed of a finite universe of items $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, each assigned a positive weight. A query specifies an admissible subset---called a slate---and the model chooses one item from that slate with probability proportional to its weight. This query model is also known as the Plackett--Luce model or conditional sampling oracle in the literature. Although MNLs have been studied extensively, a basic computational question remains open: given query access to slates, how efficiently can we learn weights so that, for every slate, the induced choice distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the ground truth? This question is central to MNL learning and has direct implications for modern recommender system interfaces. We provide both adaptive and non-adaptive algorithms for this task. Our first adaptive algorithm makes $O(\frac{n\log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ queries and learns every choice distribution in total variation distance $\varepsilon$. We also provide a second adaptive algorithm that with $O(\frac{n \log n}{\varepsilon^3})$ queries provides a stronger guarantee: each choice distribution is approximated to a multiplicative $1\pm\varepsilon$ error (except for subsets of mass smaller than $\varepsilon$). We complement these algorithms with lower bounds of $Ω(\frac{n\log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ for total variation distance and $Ω(\frac{n \log n}{\varepsilon^3})$ for the multiplicative error guarantee, showing the optimality of our adaptive algorithms. Our non-adaptive algorithm makes $O\left(\frac{n^{2}}{\varepsilon^{3}}\log n \log\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)$ queries to obtain guarantees under the multiplicative error notion. We complement this result with an $Ω(\frac{n^2 \log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ lower bound for any non-adaptive algorithm, showing that our algorithm is almost tight in $n$ (within a $\log n$ factor).

papers.title: Learn, Freeze, and Transfer an Activation Function Across Architectures

papers.title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
papers.summary: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. papers.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. papers.summary: Emerging intelligent transportation systems (ITS) show substantial benefit in reducing congestion, emissions, and accidents and enable lower-cost alternatives to highway lane expansion. papers.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
papers.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. The force may vanish at a nonzero indentation, through plasticity, an elastic aftereffect, or, under some laws with a viscous component, a load drawing the bodies apart rapidly. Such a residual indentation sits uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the law alone does not determine the interaction: because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately, as must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, both absent from the equations of motion. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex axisymmetric bodies under continuous, bounded external forces as a hybrid system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the formulation are established and formally verified in Lean 4 with the help of Claude by Anthropic. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

papers.title: Parallel Policy-Gradient Methods for Parameter Optimization of Nonlinear Feedback Controllers
papers.summary: Structured feedback controllers provide stability guarantees, but their performance depends on manually tuned parameters. Policy-gradient methods offer a systematic way to tune these parameters, but evaluating the gradient is computationally expensive because it requires a sequential forward rollout of the state dynamics followed by a backward rollout of the costate dynamics. This letter develops a time-parallel policy-gradient framework for discrete-time nonlinear control-affine systems. We evaluate the policy gradient by formulating the forward state and backward costate rollouts as residual-minimization problems and solving them with Gauss-Newton (GN) iterations that use parallel associative scans. We show that global asymptotic stability and local exponential stability of the closed loop guarantee convergence of the parallel state solver without requiring bounds on Jacobian products throughout the state space. Near the exact trajectory, GN iterations converge quadratically in a neighborhood whose size is independent of the horizon T. When initialized at the equilibrium trajectory, a clipped variant converges at a linear rate that is also independent of T. We also quantify how horizon truncation and solver tolerance affect the accuracy of the policy gradient. Experiments on an LQR problem and a lossless Lorenz-96 system with saturated passivity-based control demonstrate improved closed-loop performance and computational benefits.

papers.title: Shared-Harmonic Characterization and Robust Orientation-Selection Certification for Directional Sensing Under Anisotropic Target Motion
papers.summary: Directional sensors are often oriented using historical target trajectories, while future trajectories remain uncertain at deployment. This letter addresses two post-placement questions: i) when orientation materially affects detection and ii) when a historically selected orientation remains reliable under future target-motion shift. We develop a placement-aware framework for anisotropy-induced detection (AID), showing that orientation sensitivity is governed by harmonic modes shared by the locally visible target-direction distribution and the sensor trajectory-incidence response. The resulting AID measure admits an exact RMS interpretation for the retained-harmonic orientation response. We then introduce a sensor-induced directional discrepancy, derive a conditional bound on future orientation regret, and obtain sufficient certificates for robust orientation selection whenever the future sensor-relevant shift lies within a prescribed discrepancy radius. Using 2025 AIS ship-traffic data near Terrebonne Bay, Louisiana, historical AID is strongly correlated with held-out orientation sensitivity ($r=0.908$). Across four angular-response widths, AID explains orientation-sensitivity variation with $R^2=0.920$, compared with $R^2=0.239$ for target-only anisotropy. At the nominal threshold, 316 of 350 locations are empirically classified as orientation-useful, and all retain gain above the threshold across five held-out windows.

papers.title: PIRA: Pan-CDN Intra-video Resource Adaptation for Short Video Streaming
papers.summary: In large scale short video platforms, CDN resource selection plays a critical role in maintaining Quality of Experience (QoE) while controlling escalating traffic costs. To better understand this phenomenon, we conduct in the wild network measurements during video playback in a production short video system. The results reveal that CDNs delivering higher average QoE often come at greater financial cost, yet their connection quality fluctuates even within a single video underscoring a fundamental and dynamic trade off between QoE and cost. However, the problem of sustaining high QoE under cost constraints remains insufficiently investigated in the context of CDN selection for short video streaming. To address this, we propose PIRA, a dynamic resource selection algorithm that optimizes QoE and cost in real time during video playback. PIRA formally integrating QoE and cost by a mathematical model, and introduce a intra video control theoretic CDN resource selection approach which can balance QoE and cost under network dynamics. To reduce the computation overheads, PIRA employs state space pruning and adaptive parameter adjustment to efficiently solve the high dimensional optimization problem. In large scale production experiments involving 450,000 users over two weeks, PIRA outperforms the production baseline, achieving a 2.1% reduction in start up delay, 15.2% shorter rebuffering time, and 10% lower average unit traffic cost, demonstrating its effectiveness in balancing user experience and financial cost at scale.

papers.title: DynaSeek: Large Language Model-Driven Hybrid Dynamic Model Discovery for Grid-Tied Inverters from Limited Measurements
papers.summary: Discovering the unknown governing equations of grid-tied inverters from limited measurements is essential for the stability analysis of modern inverter-dominated power systems. papers.title: Impact of the Performance of Autonomy and Communication Subsystems on the Level-of-Safety of Partially Autonomous Machine Systems
papers.summary: The level-of-safety of a partially autonomous machine system depends on two subsystems: the autonomy subsystem that manages the system between human interventions; and the communication subsystem that enables those interventions. These subsystems are typically evaluated independently. We model the level-of-safety analytically as a function of their joint performance. Three parameters characterize the autonomy subsystem: the Mean Time Between Interventions (MTBI); the urgency $\mathcal{U}$ or mean time within which an intervention must be completed to avoid failure; and the complexity $\mathcal{C}$ or mean time to understand, decide on and execute it. Two characterize the communication subsystem: its availability $P_A$ and its latency $\varepsilon$. A dimensionless criticality ratio $ρ=(\mathcal{C}+\varepsilon)/\mathcal{U}$ prescribes the shape of the Pareto tradeoff between the MTBI and $P_A$ at a constant level-of-safety. At $ρ=0.01$, a perfect link lowers the required MTBI by two orders of magnitude. At $ρ=1$, it only halves it. Under exponential timing assumptions the model is in closed form, and compliance with a safety budget can be stated at a chosen assurance level. We illustrate it for remotely piloted aircraft with assumed parameter values and propose a simulation procedure to estimate them.

papers.title: Public Battery Field Data
papers.summary: Battery systems and algorithms are developed and evaluated primarily on laboratory cycling data, but fielded battery systems are subjected to duty cycles, temperatures, and measurement conditions that cannot be reproduced in a lab. Field data from batteries in service has begun to appear in public releases attached to individual papers, but each release has its own format, units, labels, and other gaps that make it difficult to compare against others. We present a curated collection of 37 public field-data releases from 28 research groups, covering applications that span passenger EVs, buses, light electric mobility, grid-scale storage, distributed storage, consumer electronics, industrial robotics and satellites. Where the releases are complete enough to measure, this heterogeneous collection contains 256 GB of data from at least 150,626 lithium-ion cells, 3,287 batteries, 115.6 MWh of energy storage capacity, and 3,040 unit-years of service. Critically, it also contains 957 labeled or reported faults, which provide greater visibility into what real battery performance and safety issues look like outside the lab. We release a public repository of metadata and code for each of the field datasets. For each dataset it provides a registry entry with sources, license and access links, checksums to confirm a download is complete, a metadata table, and code for how to load it. We also report where released datasets differ from their papers. We hope the collection can help serve researchers (human or otherwise) as a useful platform for improving battery field diagnostics, fault detection and health estimation. Better field evidence can also feed back to improve manufacturing quality, inform second-life screening and residual-value estimates, and broadly accelerate electrification.

papers.title: The Phases of Hierarchy
papers.summary: We develop a dynamical phase theory of hierarchy, in which depth decides whether a population of size $N$ that revises its own environment can correct it without overcorrecting. The statistics that let a large majority detect a small bias - the basis of the Condorcet jury theorem - also make its response grow as $\sqrt{N}$. Fed back into the environment it is judging, this sharpening destabilises the matched state through a flip bifurcation at a critical loop gain, which we obtain analytically for a class of models we term adaptive normal forms. We show that this instability can be attenuated by hierarchical layering, requiring a depth scaling logarithmically with $N$. This recovers known logarithmic bounds in organisational economics directly from dynamic stability conditions. Hierarchical depth carries its own costs however, and by analysing the signal chain transmission up the hierarchy we show that beyond a finite depth no correction reaches the top before its deadline, and that below it the cost of arrival grows exponentially with depth. A hierarchy that is too flat therefore oscillates and one that is too deep cannot be steered in time, leaving a bounded window of depth between an unstable flat phase and a frozen inertial phase. We further show that these results can be generalised by treating each layer as a real-space renormalisation step, classifying aggregation rules by how they transmit bias. This establishes a connection between these dynamic results to attention in Transformers, where a residual update is diffusion on the token graph and depth plays the role of scale. Finally we show these phase boundaries are observable in finite sampling, and propose measurements which may characterise the proposed phases in real adaptive systems.

papers.summary: Future wide-body all-electric aircraft require lightweight electrical distribution systems capable of delivering megawatt-scale propulsion power under demanding thermal and electrical conditions. papers.title: Global Exponential and Inverse Optimal Stabilization of a 3D Nonholonomic Vehicle in Spherical Coordinates
papers.summary: For the 3D nonholonomic vehicle actuated in surge velocity, pitch rate, and yaw rate, we construct continuous time-invariant feedback laws that stabilize both the roll-free and roll-augmented kinematic models to a target position and orientation in spherical coordinates. The design uses a spherical coordinate transformation with a singular set of codimension two and measure zero. We first present a backstepping design that yields explicit unidirectional, cusp-free feedback laws and strict barrier control Lyapunov functions (CLFs). These establish global exponential stability in spherical coordinates with user-assigned decay rates, while ensuring bounded Cartesian trajectories and exponential convergence to the target, consistent with Brockett's obstruction. The barrier terms guarantee avoidance of the coordinate singularities away from the target. The strict CLFs are then used to develop families of asymptotically stabilizing inverse optimal feedback laws for both systems that minimize a meaningful infinite-horizon cost. These laws inherit infinite gain margins from driftlessness, respect user-defined input bounds through Legendre-Fenchel transformations, and are implementable with either bidirectional or unidirectional surge actuation. Two penalty choices are illustrated: a quadratic input penalty whose associated state running cost approaches a prescribed quadratic form, and an input-constraining penalty that enforces user-defined bounds. This paper lays the foundation for constructive stabilization of the 3D nonholonomic vehicle.

papers.title: Fuel-Efficient Formation Flying via Constrained Extremum Seeking
papers.summary: This paper presents a model-free autonomous guidance architecture for minimal drag of a trailing aircraft in formation flight. Realizing the fuel savings resulting from such a formation requires learning and tracking a time-varying vortex while avoiding locations where the aircraft experiences an abrupt rolling moment disturbance. A guidance architecture for fuel-efficient safe flight, called Adaptive Plateau-seeking Optimal Guidance with ModulatEd Excitations (APOGEE), is proposed herein. Key features of APOGEE are its ability to modulate the amplitude of the excitation required to learn the unknown objective and constraint functions, to adaptively adjust the learning rates, and to keep the flight safe during the search for the optimal formation. A threshold-gated modulation reduces the amplitude of excitation when the objective function reaches an acceptably large value, thus improving flying qualities and further reducing fuel consumption. Furthermore, a Newton-based learning rule, whose estimate of the inverse of the Hessian is spectrally clamped, adapts the learning rates to the local curvature of the objective function in order to accelerate convergence and lower the chance of overshooting the optimum. Finally, a safety filter having an unknown constraint function is used to prevent a loss of control event prompted by the above mentioned disturbance. The efficacy of APOGEE is demonstrated by using a high-fidelity model of an F-16 jet and an experimentally obtained vortex model. Being model-free, APOGEE does not require modeling the dependence of the unknown functions on the characteristics of the leading aircraft, the flight condition, the crosswind, and the vortex-induced turbulence.

papers.title: Voltage-Feedback Backoff and Restoration for Priority-Based EV Charging Control

papers.title: Topology-Aware Congestion Pricing: Demand Robust Routing using the Forman-Ricci Curvature
papers.summary: Congestion pricing is widely used to improve transportation network efficiency where individual decentralized route choices can lead to system-level inefficiencies. Pigouvian tolls achieve the system optimum but depend on demand and can lose effectiveness under demand shifts, particularly on structurally critical bottleneck edges. We propose a topology-aware regularization of the Beckmann potential governing the (Wardrop) equilibrium by augmenting precomputed Pigouvian tolls with an offline structural penalty derived from Forman--Ricci curvature (FRC), which captures bottleneck structures. We prove that the resulting equilibrium is well-defined, that stronger regularization reduces flow on penalized edges, and that efficiency loss depends on how closely the structural penalty approximates optimal Pigouvian tolls. Experiments on eight real-world networks under targeted and uniform demand perturbations show reduced bottleneck flow with near-optimal efficiency. FRC achieves reductions comparable to edge betweenness at substantially lower computational cost, making it a practical, robust complement to classical congestion pricing.

papers.title: Posterior error bounds for prior-driven balancing in linear Gaussian inverse problems
papers.summary: In large-scale Bayesian inverse problems, it is often necessary to apply approximate forward models to reduce the cost of forward model evaluations, while controlling approximation quality. papers.title: Compositional Reachset-Conformant Modeling for Managing Uncertainty in the Development of Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.summary: The development of cyber-physical systems (CPS) proceeds through iterative design revisions, and compliance with safety requirements must be re-established after every revision, typically based on a system model. Conventional models, however, predict only the most likely behavior, leading to model-plant mismatch that often surfaces only during late-stage testing, when redesign is most expensive. This article presents reachset-conformant modeling as a framework for managing uncertainty throughout the development process: instead of a single trajectory, a reachset-conformant model predicts a set of behaviors, calibrated from data to conservatively enclose the true system behavior with a statistical guarantee. Safety properties established on the model therefore transfer to the realized system. Beyond a practical introduction to reachset-conformant identification and its benefits for CPS development, our main theoretical contribution is a closure result: reachset conformance is preserved under serial composition, parallel composition, and feedback interconnection, and hence under any architecture assembled from these primitives. Subsystem models identified independently from local measurements can thus be substituted into the system architecture, and the interconnected model inherits a coverage guarantee from the subsystem guarantees. We complement this result with update strategies that adapt the uncertainty sets after design changes without restarting the identification workflow. Experiments on an automotive brake-system test bench demonstrate that a) a single model covers all operating conditions and hardware variants, b) late-stage modifications are absorbed by uncertainty set updates, c) a black-box hydraulic unit is conservatively abstracted from input-output data alone, and d) independently identified subsystem models form a conformant model by construction.

papers.title: Soft projections for robust data-driven control

A computationally efficient method is proposed that separates linear control from condition-dependent nonlinear residual compensation. A finite impulse response (FIR) baseline filter is obtained through networked mean-square learning that can be made adaptive, while a multi-resolution FIR mixture-of-experts (MRF-MoE) module provides possibly nonlinear corrections. Training comprises baseline initialization, sample-graph-regularized expert and router optimization, and joint refinement. Target channels are treated as nodes in a connected network for mean-square error minimization, whereas training windows define a graph for regularizing routing probabilities. Each expert combines short-time dense and long-tail low-rank FIR filtering, and causal single-expert routing reduces inference computation. Compared with WaveNet-VNN under the same configuration, the proposed method reduces estimated inference cost by 96.3% while achieving higher NR on the test set.

papers.title: A Note on Emergent Behavior in Multi-agent Systems Enabled by Neuro-spike Communication
papers.summary: In this note, we show emergent behavior can arise even when the agents interact solely through spikes. Rather than exchanging real-valued states, each agent encodes its own state by bio-inspired neuromorphic amplifiers and transmits signed spikes, so that each firing carries a single bit and the traffic is intermittent and asynchronous. We model the resulting network as a hybrid system and introduce a coordinate that is invariant under the spike-induced jumps, which reduces the convergence analysis to a flow dynamics without jumps. On this coordinate, we prove that the agents practically synchronize and collectively follow the blended dynamics that characterizes an emergent behavior, and we derive explicit ultimate error bounds for synchronization and for the expected behavior. The bound reveals a certified accuracy--threshold trade-off and yields closed-form tuning rules under a minimum-threshold or prescribed-accuracy constraints. A distributed median solver is tested using neuro-spike communication.

papers.title: Barrier-Based Safety Filtering for Quadrotor Flight in Cluttered Environments Under Acceleration Limits
papers.summary: Accurate trajectory tracking alone does not guarantee safe quadrotor flight when the reference passes near obstacles or the available control authority is limited. This paper presents a safety-filtered trajectory-tracking framework for a quadrotor operating at a fixed altitude in obstacle-cluttered environments. A nominal tracking controller is combined with high-order control barrier constraints and an acceleration-constrained quadratic program. The safety filter preserves the nominal acceleration whenever it is admissible and modifies it only when the prescribed obstacle clearance is threatened. The analysis establishes nominal exponential tracking, forward invariance of the safe region under compatible initial conditions and continued quadratic-program feasibility, and bounded tracking error during safety intervention. Numerical experiments using an idealized planar translational model with single and multiple stationary circular obstacles show minimum clearances of $0.000$--$0.001$~m under the safety filter, compared with $-1.594/-1.421$~m under nominal control. Tracking RMSE increases from $0.618$ to $0.950$~m across reference-speed scales $0.6$--$1.6$, illustrating the effect of reference speed on tracking accuracy under safety constraints. Additional tests examine how acceleration limits affect control effort and feasibility. These findings inform safety-filter design for UAV trajectory tracking under limited control authority.

papers.title: Federated Policy Gradient for Dynamic Consensus: Gradient Dominance and Topological Bounds
papers.summary: This paper presents a federated optimization framework for dynamic consensus in homogeneous multi-agent systems. The underlying problem is challenged by the communication graph's spectral properties, which induce spatial heterogeneity and complicate decentralized control even when the dynamics of the agents are completely known. The problem is addressed in this paper by bridging distributed control theory with federated policy gradients. Accordingly, a comprehensive optimization landscape for dynamic consensus is established through a modal decomposition formulation. Specifically, a parameterized suboptimality bound is characterized that explicitly decouples the true aggregate policy gradient from the network covariance mismatch. Building on this formulation, sufficient conditions based on the graph's Laplacian spectrum are derived to recover exact gradient dominance, which guarantees convergence to the global consensus policy and establishes a lower bound on the achievable dominance coefficient. Furthermore, a Federated model-free consensus algorithm is proposed that utilizes zeroth-order exploration alongside a bisection-based discount factor annealing mechanism, successfully eliminating the need for an initial stabilizing policy. This approach achieves linear global convergence for policy optimization subroutines while maintaining strictly bounded outer iterations until dynamic consensus is achieved. Through extensive simulation studies and comparative feasibility analyses across diverse network topologies, it is demonstrated that the proposed federated approach consistently outperforms existing model-based and data-driven separation-based techniques.

papers.title: Gaussian Process Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Probabilistic Safe Set Construction
papers.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability is a general framework for verifying the safety of nonlinear systems, but it relies on an accurate dynamics model. The data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH) framework avoids system identification by lower-bounding the Hamiltonian directly from state-control-velocity data. However, it requires a Lipschitz bound on the unknown dynamics which is hard to certify from finite data, and as a single global constant this bound makes the computed safe sets conservative. We propose the Gaussian process data-driven Hamiltonian (GP-DDH), a fully data-driven framework that constructs safe sets with probabilistic guarantees under a GP prior on the dynamics. Furthermore, we suggest two methods to choose the confidence parameter $β$, both mathematically guaranteed to underbound the Hamiltonian. The computed safe set lies inside the true one with posterior probability at least $1-Δ$ for any $Δ\in(0,1)$. Numerical experiments show that GP-DDH recovers a bigger volume of the true safe set than DDH while still correctly providing a conservative approximation, even when DDH is given a Lipschitz constant computed from the true dynamics.

papers.title: Your bids are showing: re-identifying power plants in anonymized market data, and a differentially private alternative
papers.summary: ERCOT publishes every generator's hourly offer curve 60 days after the operating day. Market monitors, researchers and traders use these records to study the merit order and check for withholding. PJM publishes the same kind of data with unit names replaced by codes, on the view that masking keeps offers confidential. We test that view on ERCOT data from 2024 to 2026, where names are public and so provide ground truth, by masking the records under PJM's published rules. Public EIA and EPA data match 25% of the masked units we can score (32% of their capacity) to their plant, and 45% fall within the top five guesses. PJM's feed carries the same fields, so we expect masking to fail there too. Publishing exact fuel-group totals instead does not help. An attacker who knows the other units in a group recovers one unit's high-price offers exactly, and an outsider who knows only the target's outage dates reaches a correlation of 0.77, most of it from a few renewable and hydro units that offer at very high prices (0.32 over fossil units). We propose a differentially private release: monthly totals by fuel group and price bin, with Gaussian noise calibrated under zero-concentrated differential privacy so that each unit's whole year of offers is protected. It publishes an unbiased noisy layer and derives a monotone supply curve and shares from it at no extra privacy cost. At $\varepsilon=10$ per unit-year the market supply curve stays within 11% of the truth, the implied clearing price within \$3.0/MWh, and the attacker's correlation falls to 0.23. Whether an analysis still works depends on one ratio, how much the true quantity varies month to month against the noise, which predicts the accuracy of totals to within 0.05. The clearing price, supply slope and combined-cycle capacity remain usable, but no monthly release, private or exact, can answer questions about single hours or single units.

papers.title: Adaptive Robust Optimisation for Frequency-Constrained Market Clearing Problem
papers.summary: This paper formulates the day-ahead market clearing as a two-stage adaptive robust optimisation problem in which the first stage determines unit commitment, energy dispatch, and reserve procurement, while the second stage represents worst-case balancing actions under simultaneous uncertainty in renewable generation, load, and HVDC converter outages. Frequency security is enforced explicitly through inertia and fast frequency response constraints at the synchronous-area level, with HVDC lines allowed to provide emergency power support within their available headroom. The resulting min--max--min problem is solved by a column-and-constraint generation algorithm and applied to an eight-country North Sea test system comprising three synchronous areas, sixteen onshore bidding zones, and five offshore wind farm hubs connected through a meshed HVDC grid. We compare the Home Market (HM) and Offshore Bidding Zone (OBZ) designs on this infrastructure across different uncertainty scenarios. The results first demonstrate the value of robustness, where deterministic solutions that ignore uncertainty are severely vulnerable to worst-case realisations. Comparing the two designs, we find that OBZ's offshore zone boundaries make line congestion visible to the day-ahead market, enabling targeted reserve procurement that raises day-ahead costs but substantially reduces real-time load shedding, yielding a net reduction in total system cost that grows with the severity of localised offshore uncertainty. When both designs face the identical worst-case contingency, HM cannot distinguish an offshore converter trip from normal operation and thus fails to hedge against it, while OBZ considers the risk at the day-ahead stage. This advantage can be seasonal, scaling with the ratio of offshore wind output to HVDC line capacity and diminishing when onshore generation dominates the supply mix.

papers.title: Heterogeneous Risk-Sensitive Evolutionary Learning in Coordination Games: Polarization, Welfare Loss, and Intervention for Efficiency
papers.summary: We study evolutionary learning in coordination games in a finite population of agents with heterogeneous risk attitudes, modeled using the entropic risk measure (ERM). The population consists of two subpopulations, each with a fixed risk attitude. Under risk-sensitive best response with mutations (BRM), we characterize the long-run outcomes of the learning process. In particular, we characterize when a polarized state, in which the two subpopulations choose different actions, is uniquely stochastically stable in terms of agents' risk attitudes and the subpopulation sizes. Notably, this polarized state is strictly Pareto dominated by the payoff-dominant equilibrium under both expected payoffs and agents' own ERM-adjusted payoffs. Moreover, its welfare, measured by average expected payoff, is always lower than that of the payoff-dominant equilibrium and can also be lower than that of the risk-dominant equilibrium. Thus, heterogeneity of risk attitudes in learning alone can lead to an inefficient long-run outcome. To mitigate such inefficiency, we propose intervention mechanisms to modify agents' risk attitudes in learning. We show that a sufficiently large intervention share (the fraction of agents modified) and sufficiently high intervention intensity (the increase in their risk parameter) ensure that the payoff-dominant equilibrium is uniquely stochastically stable. However, greater intervention intensity cannot compensate for an insufficient intervention share, and a larger intervention share cannot compensate for insufficient intervention intensity.

papers.title: Connections Between Instrumental Variable, Pseudo-Linear Regression, and Prediction Error Methods in Terms of Their Minimized Criteria

papers.title: On the Effect of Bounded Rationality in Mixed Duopoly Markets
papers.summary: Nash equilibrium is a common solution concept that captures strategic interaction in market analysis. However, it assumes that all market participants are fully rational and can compute mutually consistent best responses. Level-k reasoning relaxes this assumption by modeling bounded rationality through finite reasoning depth. In this paper, we consider a variation of Cournot competition that includes two suppliers, both following level-k reasoning. One is a self-interested firm and the other serves as a benevolent social planner. First, we show that social welfare is maximized when the planner is one level more rational than its opponent. Welfare is weakly decreasing as the planner's level moves away from this optimum. We then show that welfare under bounded rationality can differ substantially from welfare at Nash equilibrium. We characterize optimal, expectation-maximizing, and robust maximin strategies for the planner under different amounts of information about its opponent's rationality level. Finally, we show how utility design can improve social welfare by allowing the planner to cooperate with or fight the self-interested firm. Numerical experiments further demonstrate and validate our findings.

papers.title: Tropical Geometry-based ReLU Lyapunov Function and Controller Synthesis
papers.summary: We investigate the joint synthesis of neural network Lyapunov functions and stabilizing controllers for systems modeled as neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs) with ReLU activations. This enables the systematic search for Lyapunov functions satisfying the desired stability conditions. Finally, we extend this framework to jointly synthesize a ReLU neural network stabilizing controller and a neural Lyapunov function, providing a unified approach to stability analysis and controller synthesis. We validate our proposed method on several nonlinear systems approximated as neural ODEs, demonstrating applications to Lyapunov function synthesis as well as joint Lyapunov function and controller synthesis.

papers.title: Towards a Formalised Framework for Analog Electronics and Circuit Theory
papers.summary: Circuit theory provides the mathematical foundation for the analysis and design of electronic circuits. papers.title: Topological Fairness in Continuous-State Systems
papers.summary: Since the early days of probabilistic programs, fairness has been used to abstract randomness in software. Intuitively, a fair scheduler reproduces the almost-sure behavior of a random choice based solely on the set of possible outcomes, independent of their (often unknown) distribution. As this abstraction attaches fairness to individual transitions, it becomes ineffective over uncountable state spaces, where every single successor has probability zero. We overcome this limitation by imposing fairness on open sets instead. This leads to the novel notion of topological fairness: every basic open set---with respect to a countable basis of the state-space topology---that lies in the set of possible successors infinitely often must be visited infinitely often. We show that topological fairness carries the intuition from program abstraction to continuous state spaces. For systems with additive stochastic disturbances, almost every trajectory is topologically fair under every control policy. Reasoning over all topologically fair trajectories is therefore a sound proof principle for almost-sure properties of the original system. Unlike in the finite-state case, however, it is not complete: topological fairness cannot capture almost-sure behavior that hinges on the relative likelihoods of disturbance outcomes. Finally, we show that topological fairness supports synthesis directly on the continuous state space. For reach-avoid objectives, we give a nested fixed point over subsets of the state space which, for a broad class of systems, computes the fair winning domain exactly together with a memoryless winning strategy. Our case studies show that this winning domain is substantially larger than the one obtained with currently available techniques, which detour through a finite abstraction and certify a winning domain that depends on the discretization in a non-monotone way.

papers.title: Closed-loop Properties of Value Iteration in Continuous Time with Approximation Errors

papers.title: Advanced Reactance Method - A Novel Approach for Distance Protection in Presence of Grid-Following Inverter-Based-Resources
papers.summary: Renewable Energy Sources and consequently inverter-based resources (IBRs) are increasing worldwide. Grid-following (GFL) IBR control is the state-of-the-art. GFL IBRs exhibit different fault behavior compared to classical synchronous generators -- particularly in terms of Fault-Ride-Through (FRT) characteristics, which are critical for grid protection relaying. Grid protection must work securely, selectively and dependably, regardless of the feeding source. As common protection algorithms are designed for fault behavior determined by synchronous generators, their performance is expected to be compromised in the presence of GFL IBRs. Distance Protection is a widely used protection algorithm at all voltage levels. Literature shows that the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs impacts the Distance Protection relaying adversely. This paper proposes the Advanced Reactance Method, a further development of the Classical Reactance Method for Distance Protection in the presence of GFL IBRs. The key idea of the proposed method is to make the algorithm independent of the feeding source impedance. Therefore, the negative sequence voltage is taken into account along with the negative sequence current. This makes the algorithm independent of the FRT behavior of GFL IBRs, even in case of suppression of negative sequence current during unsymmetrical faults. Moreover, correct settings for the classical method in the presence of GFL IBRs are presented as a solution for relays without the advanced method. The novel algorithm is evaluated against the correctly parameterized Classical Reactance Method and the Distance Protection algorithm.

papers.title: Learn Locally, Extend Globally: Koopman Eigenfunctions and the Basin of Attraction
papers.summary: Koopman eigenfunctions associated with the Jacobian eigenvalues of a stable equilibrium are Lyapunov functions defined exactly on its basin of attraction. We turn this into a computational procedure for power systems. Eigenfunctions estimated by extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) are written as functions of the state, made to vanish at the equilibrium by centering the lifted variable $\cosδ$, and verified on a grid with the model: two Lyapunov candidates from the EDMD spectrum certify up to 66\% of the basin of a single-machine infinite-bus system from data in the linear region. The Koopman semigroup property then extends the EDMD-Lie eigenfunction to the whole basin, recovered at the grid resolution with its isostables and isochrons.

papers.title: PAC Infinite-Time Safety Guarantees for Stochastic Systems with Unknown Probabilistic Distributions
papers.summary: This paper studies infinite-time safety certification for discrete-time stochastic systems with continuous dynamics and unknown disturbance distributions that have full support on a known compact disturbance set. We develop a probably approximately correct (PAC) data-driven framework that uses only finitely many i.i.d. disturbance samples: with confidence at least $1-δ$, if the certification procedure accepts a candidate certificate defining a nonempty subset of a prescribed compact safe set, then the system, starting from any state in this subset, remains within the safe set for all future times with probability at least $1-ε$. Our approach builds on a fundamental characterization of infinite-time safety. We first prove that a robust invariant set exists within a compact safe set if and only if there exists an initial state from which the system remains in the safe set indefinitely with positive probability. This reduces infinite-time safety certification to two tractable subproblems: robust invariant-set computation and finite-horizon reach-avoid certification. We first compute a robust invariant set within the safe set, then use i.i.d. disturbance samples to certify, with PAC guarantees, a subset of initial states for which the probability of reaching this set within a finite horizon while remaining safe is at least a prescribed threshold. To our knowledge, this is the first PAC framework for infinite-time safety under unknown disturbance distributions. Finally, illustrative examples demonstrate the method using semi-definite programming.

papers.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part II: Underway Docking
papers.summary: In underway directional docking, a second-order nonholonomic problem, six pairs of states of two vehicles have to be made to match by two inputs. The key challenge is to design time-invariant feedback of the relative states and the leader's measured motion only, which makes the follower's convergence in range outpaced, with no sway actuation whatsoever, by the bearing and heading convergence of the follower relative to the leader's path. We begin with nonmodular backstepping, choosing speed and commanded heading jointly to control range and bearing. Curvature compensation and normalization of angular errors by different powers of range remove the range singularity from the model. Our construction passes from unicycle kinematics to the ships' zero-sideslip points and through the sway dynamics to the physical hulls. The design extends to a leader with a different hull and to a docking point astern or abeam of the leader, where we show that, while the leader turns, a follower without sway actuation holds the point only with a heading that differs from the leader's. With strict control Lyapunov construction, we achieve global $κ$-exponential convergence, with a rate independent of the initial error.

papers.title: Control of Underactuated Surface Vessels---Part I: Stabilization in Polar Coordinates
papers.summary: A surface vessel with surge force and yaw moment as inputs and no sway actuation cannot be stabilized at a fixed pose by continuous time-invariant feedback. We introduce a zero-sideslip point, a point whose position relative to the hull depends on the surge and sway speeds and whose velocity points along the vessel's heading at every instant, and show that it moves as a unicycle. This reduction allows the time-invariant, polar-coordinate steering laws of Todorovski et al. (2025) to be applied to the underactuated vessel without modification. With two steering laws, GloBa and BoLSA, we construct strict control Lyapunov functions and prove global asymptotic stability, first for a four-state model with surge speed and yaw rate as virtual inputs, and then, by one step of backstepping, for the full six-state model with surge force and yaw moment. The analysis extends to hulls with fore-aft asymmetric sway-yaw damping, excluded in prior work by the assumption of diagonal damping. Unlike prior time-varying designs, the time-invariant controller yields smooth, non-oscillatory trajectories, an important practical advantage for docking. The designs are validated in simulation on the Cybership I hull model.

papers.title: Range-Only Dynamic Output Feedback Controller for Safe and Secure Target Circumnavigation
papers.summary: The safety and security of robotic systems are paramount when navigating hostile targets. This paper addresses the problem of circumnavigating an unknown target by a unicycle robot while ensuring it maintains a desired safe distance and remains within the sensing region around the target throughout its motion. The proposed controller design is based on a composite Lyapunov framework consisting of: (i) a quadratic Lyapunov function characterizing the target-circumnavigation objective, and (ii) a barrier Lyapunov function-based potential term enforcing the prescribed safety and sensing constraints. A notable feature of the proposed approach is that it relies exclusively on local range measurements between the robot and the target, achieved through a dynamic output-feedback controller that treats the range as the only measurable output. Using Lyapunov-based stability analysis together with an equivalent autonomous reformulation of the closed-loop dynamics, we establish asymptotic stability of the desired equilibrium while guaranteeing satisfaction of the prescribed safety and sensing constraints under the proposed controllers. Restrictive bounds on the post-design signals are also derived, and numerical simulations are presented to validate the proposed approach.

papers.title: Extended Deterministic Learning under Local Finite-Time Excitation
papers.summary: This paper develops an extension of classical deterministic learning (CDL) for the regulation of uncertain nonlinear systems, referred to as Extended Deterministic Learning (EDL). CDL relies on periodic or recurrent closed-loop trajectories to ensure that the locally active radial-basis-function (RBF) neurons satisfy a partial persistence-of-excitation (PE) condition. During regulation, however, the state approaches a constant operating point and continued excitation disappears. EDL preserves the local-learning mechanism of CDL while enabling locally accurate learning under a local finite-time excitation (local FTE) condition, which requires neither persistent excitation nor recurrent system trajectories. Specifically, an adaptive RBF controller is combined with filtered finite-time data storage. Under local FTE, the resulting scheme guarantees that all closed-loop signals are uniformly ultimately bounded, the regulation state converges exponentially to a small neighborhood of the desired operating point, and the neural weights associated with the locally active RBFs converge exponentially to small neighborhoods of their ideal values. Consequently, the unknown nonlinear dynamics are learned locally and accurately over the experienced region without requiring persistent excitation after the finite learning interval. A numerical example illustrates the improvement in local learning achieved by EDL over CDL.

papers.title: Nonlinear Moments as Equivalence Classes: A Lyapunov-Perron Approach to the Invariance Equation
papers.summary: The linear moment is well defined whenever the system and the exosystem have disjoint spectra. Its nonlinear counterpart is not: the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the invariance equation that defines it are in general not guaranteed, so additional assumptions such as Poisson stability of the exosystem and the exponential stability of the system are required to define the nonlinear moment. This paper reduces this asymmetry. By using the Lyapunov--Perron fixed-point argument, we show that under a condition called the strip condition, there exist local $\mathcal C^N$ solutions, with $N$ determined by the system and the exosystem, and every pair of $\mathcal C^1$ solutions has contact of order $k^-$, where $k$ is a spectral ratio determined by the system and the exosystem; the solutions are flat-equivalent when $k=\infty$. Based on this observation, we extend the concept of nonlinear moment as an equivalence class of functions rather than a function. The polynomial of degree $N$ or formal power series ansatz of the invariance equation are the distinguished representatives of the equivalence class. We also show that, when the system is exponentially stable, the moment describes the output shared by all trajectories up to the order $k^-$, which gives the moment a time-domain interpretation when the steady-state interpretation is not available. Finally, we show that the concept of moment matching also naturally extends as the definition of nonlinear moment is extended to an equivalence class. The ansatz also plays a crucial role in the extended notion of moment matching. The results are illustrated by a numerical example.

papers.title: Real-Time 250-kHz Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Using a Jetson AGX Orin
papers.summary: High-performance optical coherence tomography (OCT) relies on desktop workstations for data acquisition, reconstruction, and visualization, limiting integration into compact imaging systems. Although the RTX A4500 workstation achieved lower reconstruction latency, Jetson eliminated explicit host-to-device transfer and exhibited more consistent processing latency. papers.title: Frequency-Domain Identification of Passive Discrete-Time Systems via Sequential Convex Programming
papers.summary: This paper considers identification of passive discrete-time linear time-invariant systems from frequency-response data. papers.title: Loadability Assessment for Large-Load Integration: From Repeated Power Flow Tracing to Historical Trajectory Transfer
papers.summary: Integrating large data-center loads requires utilities to evaluate voltage-stability loading margins under different generation and demand conditions. Continuation power flow (CPF) traces P--V curves through successive prediction and correction steps, but related assessments can repeatedly reconstruct similar nonlinear behavior. Reusing an operating point as an initial guess does not capture the subsequent voltage response. This paper proposes a continuation method that transfers finite segments of historical power flow (PF) trajectories. Each segment is aligned with the present state and continuation direction, supplementing the CPF tangent predictor with previously computed nonlinear curve shape. Short Newton tests evaluate compatibility with the present PF equations, and an attention-based selector combines their results with network conditions, loading patterns, and recent continuation states. Numerical correction and fold refinement determine accepted solutions and the loading limit. The analysis bounds prediction error through differences in trajectory curvature and establishes sufficient conditions for local correction and branch preservation. Studies on modified IEEE 14- and 118-bus systems under renewable-generation and data-center load variations demonstrate reduced online computation and higher observed recovery of specified continuation solutions than Adaptive CPF. For loading-limit assessment, paired online speedups are 4.88--21.62$\times$ over Adaptive CPF and 1.53--4.77$\times$ over holomorphic embedding with arc-length parametrization (HEAP) across the tested scenarios.

papers.title: Algebraic Observability for Power System Dynamic State Estimation
papers.summary: Existing observability methods for dynamic state estimation are developed for ordinary differential equation (ODE) models, whereas power systems are naturally described by differential-algebraic equations (DAEs). Applying these methods generally requires a DAE-to-ODE transformation, usually Kron reduction, which may obscure the role of algebraic variables and network constraints. This paper presents an algebraic observability framework that operates directly on nonlinear power system DAEs and preserves their structure. A Jacobian rank test constructed from the model relations and their successive derivatives certifies the algebraic dependence of differential and algebraic variables on the known inputs and measurements. A reduced prolongation that differentiates only the stator relations keeps the number of latent indeterminates fixed as the prolongation order grows, which makes the test scalable. We establish the relationship between this rank test and hyper-regularity, an alternative framework for algebraic observability, and show that algebraic observability relates to local observability. We demonstrate algebraic observability on a single-machine decentralized setup, the WSCC 9-bus 3-machine system, and the IEEE 39-bus 10-machine system. The 39-bus test, with 257 latent indeterminates, completes in about 30 s.

papers.title: Control and Cryptosystem Co-Design for Encrypted Nonlinear Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.summary: A cloud that must not see the agents' states can steer them on data encrypted under CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic. Its stored estimate admits only so many multiplications before a refresh that costs time and error, and every decrypted command is flooded with noise of a mandated size, constraints no controller designed in exact arithmetic meets. For networked agents with polynomial dynamics, we prove one closed-loop bound tying the controller and the cryptosystem in both directions. If the exact loop contracts on a region, the encrypted loop stays within a certified radius of it, set by the per-cycle and refresh errors, the refresh interval, the flooding and the delay. The errors and the bound's probability are derived from the library's circuits, not measured. Inverted, the bound turns the tolerance and a failure-probability target into the refresh interval, and with it the precision, security parameters and period. Conversely, costs shape the realization: a tracing backend tallies any pipeline's operations before a ciphertext exists, and evaluating the prediction about each agent's reference holds the released error below its sixteen-agent level. A full satellite-train mission encrypted at 128-bit security ran inside its certified radius, and the certificate holds across six graphs and at 32, 64 and 128 agents. Security enters the design twice, in time and precision. The cryptosystem is therefore part of the control design, derived from the same specification and certified by the same guarantee as the controller.

papers.title: Control Barrier Functions in Motion Control
papers.summary: Projection-based controllers (PBCs) have significant engineering success in industrial high-precision motion systems by restricting their input-output behavior to performance-enhancing sector-sets thereby overcoming fundamental limitations of linear control. The projection results in continuous control signals, but their vector fields are discontinuous, potentially causing unwanted excitation of higher-order dynamics in the plant. Inspired by these projected controllers and the recent interest in control barrier functions (CBFs), we propose a new class of CBF-based motion controllers that (i) can mimic and exceed the performance benefits demonstrated by PBCs and (ii) have continuous dynamics thereby resulting in smooth control signals. We specialize our novel CBF-based control design to integrator dynamics, essentially connecting to a projected integrator, called Hybrid Integrator-Gain System (HIGS), thereby introducing CBF-HIGS. We analyze the CBF-HIGS's behavior using a describing function analysis, which reveals improved phase characteristics and a favorable trade-off in higher-order harmonic distortion compared to HIGS. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that CBF-HIGS enhances disturbance attenuation and reduces the excitation of higher-order harmonics compared to HIGS due to its continuous vector field, without compromising robustness properties. The paper provides the first use of CBFs for performance improvement of mechatronic motion systems.

papers.title: Load-Following Dynamics of an SMR-Powered All-Electric Ship with Battery Energy Storage
papers.summary: Small modular reactors (SMRs) are being considered as compact, high-energy-density power sources for future all-electric ships. In such systems, propulsion-load variations can propagate through the electrical network, turbine-generator set, steam generator, and reactor, producing coupled nuclear, thermal, mechanical, and electrical transients. This paper presents an integrated dynamic load-following analysis of an SMR-powered all-electric ship with and without battery energy storage system (BESS) support. The model couples an integral pressurized water reactor, a once-through moving-boundary steam generator, a simplified turbine model, a synchronous generator, an AC shipboard electrical network, an asynchronous propulsion motor, and a grid-connected BESS. A propulsion-load reduction is applied through the motor torque command, and the responses of the SMR-alone and SMR+BESS configurations are compared. The results show that, without BESS support, the sudden decrease in propulsion motor power creates a temporary surplus between turbine mechanical power and electrical demand, causing a large over-frequency transient and rapid steam-cycle adjustment. With BESS support, the battery absorbs excess electrical power during the transient, reducing the frequency peak from approximately 61.1 Hz to about 60.06 Hz. The BESS also indirectly smooths the upstream steam-cycle and reactor responses, including steam flow, steam-generator pressure, feedwater flow, coolant temperature, reactivity, reactor thermal power, and steam-generator region lengths. These results demonstrate the importance of modeling nuclear-powered electric ships as coupled multi-domain systems and show that BESS integration can improve short-term load-following performance.
